rules.rationale: Halogens add polarizable, weakly solvated surface with positive Hansch pi; this was the sharpest coherent subset in the previous pool.
Aromatic carbon surface transfers from water to octanol favorably; aromatic-rich scaffolds dominate high-logP chemical space.
High heteroatom count means H-bond acceptors and possible ionization, both of which raise aqueous affinity and depress logD.
Polar surface with no lipophilic compensation is the most hydrophilic regime; the two effects reinforce rather than cancel.

skills.hypothesis: Retains the best-performing direct-mechanism skill: halogen and aromatic surface raise lipophilicity while heteroatom polarity lowers it. Fails if measured logD is dominated by ionizable groups or if normalization compresses halogen effects.

rules.rationale: Source long SMILES were least soluble; the general solubility equation maps bulk onto higher logP, but the bin is crowded (2265 candidates).
Ring structure carried the largest source effect after transfer weighting; fused carbocycles add rigid apolar surface that favors octanol.
Source short SMILES were the most soluble population, so their analogues lack the hydrophobic volume needed for high measured logD.
Bulk only raises lipophilicity when polarity is absent; heteroatom-poor long skeletons are the classical high-logP regime.

skills.hypothesis: Keeps the size and ring source roles but damps their weights, since length bins are skewed and chemically heterogeneous. Fails if pool variance is driven by polarity rather than bulk.

lesson: The direct partition-mechanism skill beat the transferred size/ring skill on every development seed (mean AUC 87.92 vs 85.21, final best 90.78 vs 88.88), and per-seed variance was smaller, so esol transfer should be treated as a weak prior rather than a primary signal. Damping those source weights and keeping halogen/aromatic/heteroatom polarity terms is the safer allocation.
revision_summary: Accepted the previous selection: the halogen/aromatic versus heteroatom-polarity skill dominated on all eight development seeds, and its rules were already grounded in exact catalog values, so only the rule rationales were tightened. The competing transfer skill was not discarded but weakened, because its size and ring terms rest on a different endpoint with confidences of 0.22-0.41 and its longest bin covers more than half the pool. That skill now lowers every weight and drops the ring term further, while retaining the source-derived size and ring roles and the heteroatom-poor size interaction; it also preserves the reversal of the weakest source relation, hbond_donor_bin to hetero_atom_bin, as a negative polarity penalty. Deployment stays with the direct-mechanism skill for its higher confidence and sharper coverage of the sparse halogen and heteroatom-poor subsets.
